articles.title: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 Review: Can DC Revitalize Its Most Notoriously Convoluted Franchise?
articles.summary: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 successfully reboots a storied DC franchise, especially on the strength of its gorgeous visual storytelling. Read our full review.
body: In DC's vast catalog of superhero franchises, The Legion of Super-Heroes has always been arguably the toughest sell for casual readers. Part of that is the dorky Silver Age trappings that have persisted across the decades, but it's mostly down to the sheer size of the massive ensemble cast and the fact that the series is constantly being retooled and rebooted every few years. The very nature of DC's sliding time scale means the future is always in flux, and so we're constantly treated to a different take on this team of idealistic teen heroes.

That all being said, DC has been finding great success in revamping old properties with the DC All In/Next Level initiative, so it only makes sense that the Legion be given the same treatment. And while the prospect of rebooting this convoluted franchise yet again is a little tiresome, the results speak for themselves. This is an engaging and gorgeously rendered entry point into The Legion of Super-Heroes.
points: Legion of Super-Heroes #1 successfully reboots a storied DC franchise, especially on the strength of its gorgeous visual storytelling.

articles.title: Disney Was Working on Its Own Smash Bros.-Like Fighting Game, Confirms Ex-Concept Artist
articles.summary: Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.
body: In 2013, Christiansen posted a slew of artworks to his online portfolio, some of which showed rough sketches of various Disney characters facing off in battle. It sparked the idea that Disney had possibly toyed with a crossover fighting game — something that Christiansen has now confirmed.

Speaking with Time Extension in a September 1 interview, Christiansen opened up about the surprising way Kingdom Hearts helped bring the idea to life, though it ultimately never came to fruition. In fact, it was difficult for Kingdom Hearts to get approved in the first place, as Disney execs were hesitant to combine some of the brand’s most iconic properties.

"Since Kingdom Hearts already kind of broke that mold, producers would say, 'Hey, what if we say they're action figures, and we kind of take the same conceit as Toy Story, but have them fight each other instead?' Then, we can have all these action figures of Disney characters from Tarzan, The Lion King, and Treasure Planet, and it can be this Smash Brothers kind of thing. The title of that concept was 'Disney's Action Figure Face Off."
points: Former Disney Interactive concept artist Ken Christiansen confirmed that Kingdom Hearts inspired a Smash Bros.-like crossover fighting game that never got off the ground.

articles.title: Resident Evil Director Says There’s “No Chance” He’d Survive His Own Movie
articles.summary: Resident Evil games over the years have slowly added more fantastical elements to their tale of bioweapons running amok, but for the new live-action movie, director Zach Cregger is dialing back those ideas to a more "grounded" level.
body: "I feel like some of the Resident Evil games get a little magical," Cregger said during a Reddit Ask Me Anything session (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ).

"[Resident Evil] 8, we have a woman who can turn into a bird and fly around. And like, I love it. I've played it a bunch of times. I think it's an awesome game, but in terms of me making a movie out of it, it's like I've got to try and limit some of the wild aspects of Resident Evil. And so I chose to stick with the T-Virus, keep it as grounded as possible. So that means I'm not going to have a gigantic jacked dude in a trench coat, because I'm like, where'd the coat come from? How did he get the coat?"

Cregger explained that while the Resident Evil games do explain how Mr. X gets his stylish coat, in the world he has constructed for the movie, there's no time for the infected bioweapons to consider zombie apocalypse fashion. "This movie, it's like the outbreak just happened," Cregger added. "I want to keep it chaotic, I want to keep it primal, and I want to just keep it as grounded as I can. The T-Virus causes all kinds of cool, fun mutations. That is enough, so I'm limiting it there."

articles.title: Final Fantasy Maker Square Enix Denies Rumors That It's Going Private
articles.summary: Final Fantasy developer Square Enix has spoken out to address rumors that it's going private. Japanese business magazine Sentaku recently reported that Square Enix was looking into going private, leading to a nearly 12% increase in the company's stock price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.
body: "The September issue of the monthly magazine Sentaku carried a report regarding the possibility of Square Enix Holdings Co., LTD. (the 'Company') going private. However, this information was not announced by the Company," Square Enix said in a statement. "No consideration is currently being given within the Company to taking the Company private."

The news comes amid wider consolidation across the gaming industry. EA was recently acquired by a Saudi Arabian investment group and taken private, which has led to concerns from both fans and EA employees about what its new owners will do. Will they continue to invest in single-player games from BioWare and leverage beloved IP like Dead Space, or will they go heavy on microtransactions and live-service games? It'll be a while before we can really see the effects of the acquisition and EA's decision to go private, but naturally, a report like this for Square Enix can lead to rampant speculation about the company's future.

articles.title: This Horror Game Is Having A Dino Crisis Of A Different Sort
articles.summary: Athanasia, the indie horror game that traps you in a mysterious facility full of dinosaurs, is launching in the ideal horror-game window: just before Halloween. GameSpot can exclusively reveal Athanasia's release date; it comes to PC on October 19 via Steam Early Access.
body: In Athanasia, players find themselves trapped in a South American research facility swarmed by dinosaurs that have somehow traveled through time to the present day in the game's story. Though the art style recalls something quite like Dino Crisis, Capcom's long-dormant dino horror series, the specifics of the gameplay are actually more surprising.

Influenced by System Shock, the first-person Athanasia also has immersive-sim leanings, as seen in the game's trailer below, where the player can creatively get themselves out of a jam by experimenting with their environment. Of course, if it's really an immersive sim, players will be able to flush the toilets. It's wait-and-see on that one.
That's not the only wrinkle, though. Athanasia also teases a different enemy type hidden from all of the game's trailers so far. It seems something worse than dinosaurs is lurking.
Athanasia launches on October 19 from Momentum Games, with the horror-focused Black Lantern Collective publishing.

articles.title: DC Villains 6-Film Limited Edition Steelbook Collection Glows in the Dark
articles.summary: Some of the best DC superhero movies going back five decades are collected in a new 4K steelbook library case bundle. It’s called the limited-edition DC Villains 6-Film collection, and it features movies starring Superman, Batman, Aquaman, and more.
body: The collection is up for preorder for $139.99 exclusively at Amazon, with a release date of October 27.

The movies range from the 1979 Christopher Reeves classic Superman: The Movie to Matt Reeves' 2022 masterpiece The Batman. Those movies are great, as are the four in between, including the two Tim Burton Batman films. See the full list of movies included below.

While the movies are obviously the main focus here, including the iconic villains the heroes fight, the packaging is also a key component of the collection. Each of the six movies has its own steelbook case, with the movie poster on the cover. If you put the cases under a light and then turn off the lights, you’ll see glow-in-the-dark graffiti scrawled across each of the steelbooks. It’s a pretty cool idea.

The six steelbooks are housed in a library case that offers plenty of room and protection for the individual discs. The library case itself is also decked out in glow-in-the-dark markings. You can get an idea of what it looks like in the photo above (or in the listing itself on Amazon).

articles.title: How The Resident Evil Movie Borrows From RE4 And RE7
articles.summary: Ahead of the release of Resident Evil later this month, director Zach Cregger sat down for an Ask Me Anything session on Reddit he answered questions about the movie. While trailers for Resident Evil have teased a few Easter eggs that players of the game will recognize, Cregger also spoke about…
body: "I feel like the biggest inspiration for this was the games, and I mean cinematically," Cregger said during the AMA (via YouTuber Troy Hill Talks Movies ).

Cregger added that he choreographed scenes to emulate this gameplay approach, so as to "train the viewer" early on as to how they're going to experience the movie and the journey of Bryan, the medical courier played by Austin Abrams. Resident Evil 7 was also influential on the film for how it portrayed a normal person being put through the ringer, Cregger said, but Resident Evil 4 also played a large role in the "rhythm" of the film.

"[Resident Evil] 4 has the rhythm that I really like, where you're moving from set piece to set piece, location to location," Cregger explained. "Resident Evil 4 is just such a big game. You go through all these different worlds, from the village to the castle, and to the island. It just kind of keeps giving and giving. I like the idea of kind of borrowing the rhythm and the scale from RE4 and using some of the character elements from RE7."
Resident Evil hits theaters on September 18, and Cregger has teased a fast-paced movie full of "f**ked up and weird" imagery for fans to enjoy.

articles.title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Just Got A Surprise Free Update With 8-Player Split-Screen
articles.summary: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe has been Nintendo's golden goose for several years, as it's the company's best-selling Switch game of all time and has received various updates over the years, becoming a feature-packed experience.
body: Alongside the new mode that segments your TV like a slab of chocolate, Mario Kart 8 Deluxe Version 4.0.0 also adds several more improvements that take advantage of the increased horsepower on Switch 2. In a nutshell, you're getting sharper graphics, CameraPlay support, and shorter load times in addition to smaller quality-of-life tweaks under the hood of the popular kart-racing game. Even player speed has been increased by a whopping coin--whatever that means.

But the expanded local split-screen is the real star of the show here, as not only can you strain your eyes while playing on TV, but you can also make your local optometrist happy by watching all those races unfold in handheld mode on the Switch 2. Considering just how much of an intensive load it is to render eight sessions in real time, the new multiplayer mode is a technical marvel to watch.

articles.title: Brütal Legend Is Still Double Fine's Best Game, Sequel or Not
articles.summary: Double Fine’s new $400K Kickstarter has a stretch goal that reads like either a dare or a joke, I can’t decide which: Raise $100 million for the studio’s upcoming Amnesia Fortnight game jam, and the studio will make Brütal Legend 2.
body: That’s fabulous, we love to see new games being made, a crowdsourced upwelling of affection for a rad IP will always get me, and I get the dopamine of seeing a progress bar creep to the right, but I think this distracts from the bigger picture: Since the perfect Brütal Legend game already exists, do we need a sequel? Do we really want a sequel? Or is it time to admit that despite any very publicized crowdfunding goals, we’re probably not getting one? Admitting this would free us up to play Double Fine’s best game again, which is the ideal outcome here, because the first and only Brütal Legend was a wild ride.

articles.title: 10 Years Later, Pokémon Go Is Officially Getting Some Love from the Pokémon Anime
articles.summary: A decade later, Pokémon Go is still going strong, and Professor Willow is finally getting some recognition from the long-running Pokémon anime series. The Pokémon Company announced on X that the multi-billion dollar mobile game hit is getting a crossover with the ongoing Pokémon Horizons anime.
body: The news came with a trailer showing a Pokémon Go player capturing the Charmander from the anime, which has a pair of goggles.

As listed on the Pokémon Go website, players will be able to capture an exclusive Charmander that’s wearing Friede’s goggles. The ‘mon keeps its accessory even as it evolves into Charmeleon and Charizard. As for other event bonuses, Tier 1 of the Go Pass unlocks 2x candy for catching Pokémon, Tier 2 makes it so that Regular Lure Modules last for one hour and may attract the featured Pokémon, and Tier 3 grants additional Stardust for catching Hatenna and Wattrel.

One-Star Raids will feature Pikachu wearing Cap’s hat, and Three-Star Raids will have the event-exclusive Charizard, Meowscarada, Skeledirge, and Quaquaval. The crossover event runs from Sept. 16 at 10 a.m. to Sept. 22 at 8 p.m. local time.

articles.title: Iconic Banjo-Kazooie composer is more hopeful about a sequel these days, but knows "like three companies" have already been turned down
articles.summary: Grant Kirkhope - the iconic video game composer behind the Donkey Kong Rap and the Banjo-Kazooie games - thinks a potential Banjo-Threeie is slightly more likely now.
body: Almost three decades have passed since Banjo-Kazooie's last mainline platformer flapped onto the N64 and it's been almost 20 years since Banjo-Kazooie: Nuts and Bolts flopped onto the Xbox 360, but it's never too late for another adventure with the bird and bear.

Speaking to FRVR, Kirkhope explained that he used to feel there was "zero chance of another Banjo-Kazooie game." Nowadays, that sentiment's been upgraded to a "slight chance" because he thinks Rare's updated leadership could be more receptive to an outside developer spearheading a threequel.

"Rare just typically say no to everything," the composer explained. "I've known people present cartoons to them, all sorts of ideas, and they just say no to everything." But since former studio head Craig Duncan stepped down from his role at Xbox Game Studios, Kirkhope reckons Rare might be "a little bit different right now" and "a bit more open to discussion."

articles.title: 1001: Threads of Mizan Was One of Gamescom 2026’s Best Action Games
articles.summary: 1001: Threads of Mizan was, as game director Scott Lussier said to me in an interview at Gamescom 2026, the "greatest secret ever kept." The gaming industry has a habit of leaking news about upcoming games and therefore spoiling the surprise, so when the trailer for Mizan was shown during Opening…
body: The only problem with the reveal trailer was that while it wears its Arabian Nights inspiration on its sleeve, it gave no indication as to its genre, mission structure, story, and so on. I've played the game now, in a 15-minute session behind closed doors. While I only got to experience a brief section of one level, Lussier also explained how the rest of the game will work.

"What we're building here is a single-player action adventure game that gets better with your friends," he told me. "We have created our own world that is inspired largely by the tales of Arabian folklore, and we're weaving the world of Arabian Nights inside there. It's about flying on carpets, fighting colossal enemies, and doing it with your friends while also experiencing stories inside of stories."

…but it does have another dynamic in play: flight combat. After we took down the Sand Knight, a mini-boss that required plenty of synergy between our trio to dodge his attacks and pummel him together when he was staggered, the demo flung us directly into the headline act, a boss fight against a jinn named Nazjush.

articles.title: 'Avengers: Doomsday' Directors Officially Comment on Why They Filmed Without a Final Script
articles.summary: Avengers: Doomsday is coming to movie theaters this December and Marvel Studios hopes it will get the Marvel Cinematic Universe back on track, following a handful of whiffs like The Marvels, Captain America: Brave New World, and Thunderbolts*.
body: But the Doomsday directors started shooting without a finished script after Marvel pivoted from its Kang the Conqueror storyline in response to controversy surrounding actor Jonathan Majors. In a new interview, the Russos weighed in on why they began filming without a final script, relying on on-set decisions.

“We always view the script as a living organism. We’re improvisation-based, rehearsal-based directors. We like to see what the actors bring to the characters, and sometimes you don’t get the actors until a few days or few weeks before you shoot them. And a lot of the time, that’s when the magic happens.”

With Avengers: Doomsday fast approaching, a major concern is that the film began shooting before the script was finished. While it isn’t unprecedented for Hollywood movies to start filming without a complete screenplay, this situation can often lead to disjointed, poorly plotted films. It doesn’t help that the circumstances around Doomsday don’t seem ideal.

articles.title: Mario Kart 8 Deluxe gets a surprise Switch 2 update, bringing eight-player split-screen to the evergreen racing game
articles.summary: Nintendo heard us. Our Mario Kart 8 Deluxe parties weren't simultaneously ruining enough friendships, so the evergreen racer can now be played in split-screen with up to eight players thanks to a surprise Switch 2 update.
body: Nintendo last night added Mario Kart 8 Deluxe to the list of games that now enjoy free Switch 2 updates. The surprise patch includes improved image quality and faster loading times when playing Mario Kart 8 on Switch 2 consoles, alongside support for GameShare and CameraPlay - meaning you can watch your soon-to-be ex-friends shout expletives as you spam them with red shells, as long as you're playing with two-to-four players.

But the headlining feature is easily the ability to play with up to eight people on the same console. Before this week, Mario Kart 8 only supported four players locally, but that limit can now be doubled. You just need to be playing on a Switch 2 and have at least one Joy-Con 2 or Nintendo Switch 2 Pro Controller connected. I'm not sure how legible Mario Kart 8 might be when the TV's sliced eight ways, but a little more chaos can't hurt, right?

A few more minor changes are also buried at the bottom of Nintendo's patch notes. Booster Course Pass owners now have a '96 Races' option when creating custom VS matches, you'll no longer be slowed down when Boo goes off to steal an enemy's item, and all racers now go a little faster "by the equivalent of one coin."

articles.title: Lego Skylines is already looking like a treat, but I suspect the real magic's in the stuff Paradox won't talk about just yet
articles.summary: How's this for an unhelpful opener: in a lot of ways, Lego Skylines is exactly what you think it is; but in others, it's probably not. Conceptually, it's a winner, of course - a city builder built with Lego! - and yet it takes things unexpectedly far.
body: Let me explain! You've probably seen Lego Skylines' trailer, and the obvious assumption is that Paradox is pitching it as a sort of stripped down, ultra-accessible My First Cities Skylines (developer Iceflake, if you weren't aware, is the current steward of the franchise, following original studio Colossal Order's ousting amid a disastrous run for Cities Skylines 2 ). And as my 45-minute hands-on begins, that's exactly what Lego Skylines feels like.

It's a wonderfully characterful, colourful thing that starts with a boat ride to an untouched island on my first day as a Master Builder. Almost immediately my skills are in demand, and I'm asked to build a house for a family keen to make the island their home. That unlocks a range of 'small home' prefabs - a traditional suburban house, a ranch-style abode, and so on - that I can select then plop into the world, the building satisfyingly assembling itself in a quick brick-by-brick flurry.
points: How's this for an unhelpful opener: in a lot of ways, Lego Skylines is exactly what you think it is; but in others, it's probably not.

points: Don't miss the Great Sword Boosted Action Trailer for Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, an upcoming expansion to the hit third-person monster hunting game developed by Capcom.
Players can get a look at the new Boosted Action mode for the Great Sword, a state that allows for more powerful attacks in the heat of battle.
Gain the upper hand against any monster with the Boosted Great Sword in Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance, launching in 2027 for PlayStation 5 (PS5), Xbox Series X|S, and PC (Steam).
videos.author: IGN

videos.title: Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance - Boosted Action Overview | PS5 Games
videos.summary: Ascend to Master Rank with the Boost Bracer, a new hunting action that expands the abilities of each of the 14 weapon types in Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.
body: Build Boost Bracer energy by staying aggressive with your attacks, then activate Boost with a special Boost Driver attack, or other unique actions per weapon. Boost enables abilities such as new combos and enhanced attacks, allowing you to seize control of the powerful threats that await you.
*Footage represents a game still in development. The main Monster Hunter Wilds game is required to play Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.
About Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance
points: Ascend to Master Rank with the Boost Bracer, a new hunting action that expands the abilities of each of the 14 weapon types in Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.
Build Boost Bracer energy by staying aggressive with your attacks, then activate Boost with a special Boost Driver attack, or other unique actions per weapon.
The main Monster Hunter Wilds game is required to play Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance.
Monster Hunter Wilds: Ascendance takes the hunt to new heights in Master Rank.

videos.title: Teardown - Multiplayer Update | PS5 Games
videos.summary: This update turns Teardown into a fully destructible playground for up to 12 players. Team up to tackle the campaign in co-op, jump into competitive modes like Deathmatch and Capture the Flag or unleash pure creative chaos in Sandbox Mode across every map.
body: With 70+ multiplayer-ready community mods already live and more being added, the possibilities are nearly limitless. New game modes, custom maps, wild rule sets and experimental tools.
points: This update turns Teardown into a fully destructible playground for up to 12 players.
